A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework, renamed from NetPress to NetArena. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison across the retained applications and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on capacity planning, routing troubleshooting, and Kubernetes policies, plus supervised fine-tuning and a preliminary reinforcement-learning experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports an RL reward trajectory and concrete agent failure examples.

M1.justification: The state-action abstraction, constructive and reactive query generation, ground-truth construction, and emulator-based evaluation remain unchanged. The new extension guide documents how to instantiate the existing framework rather than introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same capacity-planning topology, Mininet routing faults, and Kubernetes microservice-policy tasks. Appendices B–D retain their operational and fault coverage; proposed extensions and adversarial applications do not constitute additional evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: The five GPT-4o/Qwen2.5-72B agents, SFT variants, and untuned RL control are retained. New Table 1 summarizes other benchmarks; it does not report additional comparator agents evaluated on NetArena's tasks.

E3.justification: The small/large query counts remain 100/5000 for CP, 150/2250 for Routing, and 150/2000 for K8s. SFT subset sizes, model sizes, environment configurations, and evaluation metrics are also retained. Reworded prompts and redrawn axes do not establish changed experimental procedures.

E4.justification: New Table 2 adds examples of safety violations, control-logic errors, and operational errors across the three tasks. Figure 6 adds training-dynamics and command-output analysis to the existing RL experiment; the main complexity breakdown and SFT generalization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains Bernoulli standard errors and 95% confidence intervals calculated as p ± 1.96 SEM. No new repeated-run, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported; Table 1 adds summary entries rather than a new statistical practice.

E6.justification: Figure 6 newly reports the RL reward trajectory through 100 episodes, a stated learning transition around episode 36, and before/after command examples. Table 1 adds benchmark-summary figures and Table 2 adds qualitative failures. The matched benchmark and SFT values in Figures 3–5 are retained after accounting for rescaling and reordered labels.

T1.justification: The state-transition system, constructive composition, fault injection, correctness definition, and per-step safety formulation in Equations 1–5 retain their mathematical substance. No new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain dynamically generated network benchmarks, executable ground truths, controllable complexity, and evaluation of correctness, safety, and latency. v2 foregrounds quantitative findings and SFT/RL uses already discussed in v1 without materially redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 5.3 explicitly rejects equating emulator success with deployment readiness and identifies noisy observability, operational drift, heterogeneous tooling, and hidden dependencies as transfer limitations. The RL discussion also adopts more qualified language about initial feasibility and potential self-improvement.

D1.justification: v2 replaces Appendix A's hardware specification, including four 80GB A100 GPUs and CUDA 12.8, with application-extension guidance and a six-step construction table. It also supplies a project website. Most detailed environment, prompt, and evaluation documentation in Appendices B–D is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including ITBench, MeshAgent, Dysca, and a survey of dynamic evaluation, while removing DyVal-2 and several background references. New Table 1 makes the comparison with existing network benchmarks explicit, but the central positioning against small, static benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the main explanatory and discussion text are rewritten and condensed. The framework and title are renamed, terminology and headings are revised, prompts are reorganized, and extension and deployment-generalization sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables and the two-panel RL figure. Figure 4 is substantially redrawn with abbreviated labels, differentiated line styles, reordered K8s axes, and tighter radial ranges. Prompt and emulator-output boxes are restyled, Figure 1 is relocated, and the document adopts the conference layout.

improvement.justification: The added failure examples, inspectable RL trajectory, extension guidance, and explicit deployment limitations make the existing work easier to assess and apply. These provide a modest overall gain, partly offset by removal of the hardware specification and new reporting ambiguities: Table 1 pairs 44% correctness with an unexplained [0.01, 0.14] entry under its 95% CI heading. The core experimental validation remains largely unchanged.
